title: Prime-to-ell residue degree after arbitrary field extension
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $L/k$ a finite field extension of degree $d$ [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $\ell$ be a prime with $\ell\nmid d$, and let $K/k$ be any field extension. Form the scheme
$$P=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$$
[def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Every point $z$ of $P$ has $[\kappa(z):K]$ finite, and at least one such point has $\ell\nmid[\kappa(z):K]$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The residue fields are those of $L\otimes_k K$, where the tensor algebra has multiplication $(a\otimes b)(a'\otimes b')=aa'\otimes bb'$. No separability or finiteness assumption is imposed on $K/k$.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.2.7, printed pp. 25--26: its field-theoretic assertion, with arbitrary extension K/k; separate the separable and purely inseparable parts.
